name: Lake Issyk-Kul
dist: The shoreline runs through five districts
near: The catalog point is in the middle of the lake; the nearest shores are Cholpon-Ata / Bosteri (north shore, ~20 km) and Tamga / Tosor (south shore). The main towns on the lake: Cholpon-Ata, Karakol (12 km from the eastern shore), Balykchy (west).
elev: 1607–1608 m above sea level (Sputnik8: 1608 m; the commonly accepted value is 1607–1609 m, and the level fluctuates from year to year).
short: The world's second-largest high-mountain lake that never freezes (6,236 km², up to 668 m deep, 1607 m above sea level), lying between the Kungey and Terskey Ala-Too ranges. It is Kyrgyzstan's main resort region, with a beach season from late June to mid-September.
desc: Issyk-Kul (“warm lake”) is an endorheic, slightly brackish (5.9 ‰) lake 182 km long and up to 58 km wide, with a 688 km shoreline and a volume of 1,738 km³ (CAIAG). About 80 rivers flow in and none flows out; because of its salinity and depth the lake does not freeze in winter. In summer the water warms to 19–25 °C (22–25 °C near the shore in July–August). The north shore (Cholpon-Ata, Bosteri, Chok-Tal) has sandy beaches, pansionats (Soviet-style resort hotels) and lively holidays; the south shore (Tamga, Kadji-Sai, Bokonbaevo) is quieter, with canyons and yurt camps; the east has Karakol and the gateway to Terskey Ala-Too. The lake and its basin are part of the Issyk-Kul UNESCO biosphere reserve. Pleasure boats and yachts sail from Cholpon-Ata (500 som for 1–1.5 h, 2024), and the shores have petroglyphs, Ruh Ordo, Kyrchyn and hot-spring baths.
guide: First choose a shore: the north if you want a beach, a pansionat and nightlife; the south if you want quiet, canyons and yurts; Karakol if you are here for the mountains. Don't only look at the lake from the beach: a two-hour boat trip from Cholpon-Ata with a swim in deep water costs ~500 som and runs from mid-June to mid-September. The water is 22–25 °C in July–August, but the sun at 1,600 m is harsh — you will burn in an hour. Beaches at pansionats are often paid (200–300 som); wild ones are free. June and September are quiet and cheaper, and the water is still/already good for swimming.
see: North shore: the beaches of Cholpon-Ata and Bosteri, the Cholpon-Ata petroglyphs, Ruh Ordo, the Grigorievka and Semyonovka gorges. South shore: Skazka (Fairy Tale) Canyon, Manjyly-Ata, Barskoon, Jeti-Oguz, the beaches of Tamga and Kadji-Sai, and Bokonbaevo with its eagle hunters (berkutchi). East: Karakol, the Przhevalsky museum at the Pristan (port) area. Boat and yacht trips on the water; sunsets over the lake.
skip: You expect a warm sea: even in August the water is rarely above 25 °C. You are coming in October–May for the beach — the season is closed and only sanatoriums and the mountains are open. You want solitude on the north shore in July–August — there is none.
diff: Not applicable to the lake as a whole; beaches and boat trips have no restrictions; for mountain routes, see the gorge cards.
when: Beach season is late June to mid-September (freedom-travel.kz, 2026; Sputnik8: June–September, peak July–August); June and September have fewer people and lower prices. In winter: skiing in Karakol and the sanatoriums; the lake does not freeze.
hours: There is no single schedule: pansionat beaches are open in daytime and cost from 200–300 som (2026); boats from Cholpon-Ata run from 15 June to 15 September, with daytime trips and evening “parties”. For the hours of specific places, see their cards.
daytime: Swim after 12:00, when the water and air have warmed up; for photos, sunset on the north shore (the sun sets behind Kungey) and sunrise on the south; evening boat trips last 2 h.
how: From Bishkek: marshrutkas (minibuses) from the new bus station (Koltsevaya/Alma-Atinskaya; the Western bus station has been closed since late 2024): to Balykchy 300 som, to Karakol 450–500 som (Kaktus.media 04.2024; Destination Karakol), to Cholpon-Ata ~4 h; shared taxi to Karakol 1000–1500 som, private taxi to Cholpon-Ata ~7000 som, to Karakol ~11,000 som (Sputnik8, 11.2025). From Almaty: bus to Balykchy ~$4, transfer $100–150, flight Almaty — Tamchy (FlyArystan, seasonal). Issyk-Kul airport (Tamchy) gets charter flights in summer.
needcar: To move between shores — yes (the loop around the lake is ~440 km); marshrutkas run along the shore on the A363 highway Balykchy — Cholpon-Ata — Karakol and on the southern road Balykchy — Bokonbaevo — Karakol.
self: Yes, fully: the road around the lake is paved, marshrutkas run, and no permits are needed (the border zone is only in the upper reaches of the Sary-Jaz/Inylchek and near Kegen — not at the lake).
roadtype: Paved road all the way around the lake (A363 in the north, the southern road Balykchy — Karakol); the southern road is worse in places. Access roads to the gorges are dirt roads / 4×4.
traveltime: Bishkek — Balykchy ~3 h; — Cholpon-Ata ~4 h; — Karakol 5–7 h (marshrutka) / 5–6 h (taxi) (Destination Karakol 2024, Sputnik8 2025). Almaty — Issyk-Kul by car ~8 h.
stay: 2026 (freedom-travel.kz): north shore — 3–4* hotels $80–150/night at peak, guesthouses $50–80, budget $30–45; south shore — yurts/glamping $40–70, guesthouses $40–60; hostels $10–25 per bed. Sputnik8: budget $8–10, mid-range $15–20, premium $50–90 (outdated benchmarks). For specific places, see the town cards.
net: All three operators cover the coast (Beeline KG, MegaCom, O!); since 2019 MegaCom has 4G in Cholpon-Ata, Balykchy, Karakol, Bokonbaevo and Ananyevo; in 2024–2026 Beeline is putting up new base stations in resort villages (Ornok, Chok-Tal, Kojoyar, Kyrchyn). There is no signal in the gorges. Tourists recommend Beeline/MegaCom (freedom-travel.kz, 2026) or O! (eurasia.travel).
entry: There is no single entrance. Paid beaches at pansionats cost 200–300 som (freedom-travel.kz, 2026); wild beaches are free. A boat trip costs 500 som (2024).
transfer: Marshrutka Bishkek — Karakol 450–500 som (2024), — Balykchy 300 som (2024), — Bokonbaevo 550–650 som (2025); shared taxi to Karakol 1000–1500 som (2024); taxi Bishkek — Cholpon-Ata ~7000 som, — Karakol ~11,000 som (2025); Almaty — Issyk-Kul transfer $100–150 (2026).
bring: SPF 50 sunscreen and a hat (1,600 m, strong UV), swimsuit, a light jacket for the evening (nights are +10–15 °C even in summer), cash in som (cards are not accepted everywhere), water shoes for the pebble beaches of the south, warm clothes for trips into the mountains.
warn: The strong high-altitude sun burns you within an hour. The water is cool and gets cold quickly with depth; swimming in a storm is dangerous. Boats only with life jackets. Prices in season go up 1.5–2 times; on weekends the north shore has traffic jams and a shortage of rooms. Ticks in the gorges in May–June. The border zone is only far from the lake (upper Sary-Jaz); no permits are needed on the coast.
food: Smoked and fried fish from stalls along the highway and at bazaars (chebak/roach, farmed trout), ashlyan-fu in Karakol, beshbarmak and kumys in yurts, fresh apricots and apples on the south shore (July–August), honey. Specific eateries have not been checked.
reviews: Google Maps “Issyk-Kul”: 4.7/5, 2,690 ratings (03.10.2026). Typical pluses from 2025–2026 guides and reviews: clean water, views of snowy ranges, variety of shores; minuses — cool water, seasonal prices, crowds and litter on the north shore in August, service in old pansionats.
p.sum: First choose a shore. The north (Cholpon-Ata, Bosteri, Chok-Tal) has beaches, pansionats and boats, 4–5 h from Bishkek on the A363; the south (Bokonbaevo, Kadji-Sai, Tamga, Tosor) has quiet, yurts and canyons, 5–6 h. The easiest way to get there is a marshrutka/GoBus from the Bishkek bus station (400–600 som), in summer by train Bishkek-2 → Balykchy (daily from 26.06 to 13.09.2026, from 150 som); from Kazakhstan by FlyArystan flight to Tamchy or via the Kegen — Karkyra border crossing to Karakol. The loop around the lake (~440 km) is fully paved, and marshrutkas run along both shores.

p.onsite.camping: On the wild beaches of the south shore you can pitch a tent freely (Tamga, Tosor, Kadji-Sai); at Bel-Tam a tent pitch is $3. On the north shore almost the whole coast is taken by pansionats. The lake is a UNESCO biosphere reserve: take your litter with you.

p.season: Late June to mid-September is the beach season, water +22–25 °C; July–August is the peak of prices and crowds (June and September are 20–40% cheaper); boats 15.06–15.09; train 5.06–13.09; flights to Tamchy mid-June to late August; World Nomad Games — Kyrchyn, 1–6.09.2026. October–May: sanatoriums and skiing in Karakol (December–March); the lake does not freeze. Ticks in the gorges in May–June.
p.budget.economy: Marshrutka 400–600 or train 150–180; guesthouse/hostel 500–1,000; food 600–1,000; beach 0–300. ≈ 1,500–2,500 som/person/day.
p.budget.comfort: Taxi 1,000–1,500 per seat or a car for 7,000; pansionat 1,650–3,000 with meals or a 4* hotel ~$83–105 (~7,000–9,000); boat 500; excursion 700–900. ≈ 6,000–12,000 som/person/day.
p.permits: Not needed: there is no border zone on the coast (the border zone is in the upper reaches of the Ak-Suu district, Inylchek/Merzbacher). When entering from Kazakhstan — regular passport control at Kordai or Kegen — Karkyra.
p.access: Very accessible: flat beaches, pansionats with meals, medical sanatoriums; for wheelchairs — the promenades and grounds of large pansionats, but not the wild beaches. With children — July–August (warm water), but the sun is harsh. With dogs — many pansionats do not allow them, so check; wild beaches are fine.
